products.title: The Cloud, Locally Hosted
products.tagline: Five-bay cloud storage that cannot be sunset, throttled, or fondly discontinued.
description: The flagship object of the Local Copy Department: a soft, translucent 3D-printed cloud that holds five USB drives in spring-grip bays. Push a drive in; the cloud grips it; your files remain exactly where you left them, indefinitely, which is apparently a premium feature now.
Flexible TPU body with hand-pressed lettering, 2026. No account, no renewal email, no deprecation roadmap. Uptime is enforced by physics.

Stands on a desk like a small monument to ownership, straps to a shelf or rack post with zip ties, or screws straight into drywall through its mounting slots — all three demonstrated, none requiring a support ticket.
Ships with the complete deployment kit: three zip ties and two #8 screws with drywall anchors. Every supported mounting posture, zero trips to the hardware store.

Approximately 167 × 97 × 34 mm. Fits full-size USB-A sticks and anything smaller; the flexible bays self-adjust. Ships as shown in warm white with blue lettering. Drives not included — those are your files, and that is the entire point.
